question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: He saw a most wonderful sight.

A. In every tree that he could see there was a little child.

B. The birds were flying about and twittering with delight.

C. And the trees were so glad to have the children back again that they covered themselves with blossoms.

D. Through a little hole in the wall the children had crept in.

S2: It was a lovely scene, only in one corner it was still winter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, A, C, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Children entering, filling the trees, and the resulting joyful scene.

• D (explains part of the ‘wonderful sight’ in S1 — how the children arrived) → A (continues describing the sight, now showing where the children (D) had gone) → C (the trees' (‘they’) reaction to the children now settled in them (A)) → B (continues the joyful scene from C)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• The trees reacting joyfully must follow the sentence that places the children in the trees.

 

NOTE

• C's ‘the trees... covered themselves with blossoms’ only follows once the children are in ‘every tree’ (A).

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: The sailor took home his gold, made his ship ready, and then, taking leave of his wife and sons, he went down to the shore, where he found the old man waiting for him with a slave and twenty ass-loads of empty sacks.

A. For this the old man steered, and they soon landed upon it.

B. This they reached after some hours of travel and climbed to the summit, upon which they found a broad plain where more than two hundred pits had been dug.

C. Having loaded his slave with some sacks, the old man with his companions set out towards a mountain which they could see in the distance.

D. Taking a particular star for their mark, they sailed for three months, when an island appeared to one side of them.

S2: The old man then explained to the sailor that he was a merchant and that he had, on that spot, found a mine of jewels.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, A, C, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The voyage, landing, and journey to the mountain of pits.

• D (continues the journey after they set out, described in S1) → A (‘this’/‘it’ refers to the island just named in D) → C (a new stage of action after landing in A) → B (‘This’ refers to the mountain named in C)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘This’ and ‘it’ as opening words always point to the noun of the immediately preceding sentence.

 

NOTE

• B's ‘This they reached’ refers to ‘a mountain’ named only in C, so C must precede B.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: And addressing another eunuch, he said to him, O my chief, as thou hopest for Allah’s protection, tell me, am I the Prince of the Faithful?

A. And Abou Hassan, perplexed at all that he beheld, said, In one night do I become Prince of the Faithful!

B. He remained perplexed and confounded until the morning, when a eunuch advanced to him and said to him, May Allah grant a happy morning to the Prince of the Faithful!

C. Yea, by Allah, answered the eunuch; thou art at this present time the Prince of the Faithful and the caliph of the Lord of all creatures.

D. Was I not yesterday Abou Hassan, and today am I the Prince of the Faithful?

S2: And he handed to him a pair of shoes of gold stuff, reticulated with precious stones and rubies; and Abou Hassan took them, and after examining them a long time, put them into his sleeve.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, A, D, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The eunuch's confirming answer, followed by Abou Hassan's bewildered reaction.

• C (the eunuch's direct answer to the question posed in S1) → A (Abou Hassan's astonished reaction to the answer just given in C) → D (continues his bewildered questioning from A) → B (describes his (‘He’) continuing confusion, following his questions in A and D)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A direct answer to a question typically comes first, before the reaction to that answer.

 

NOTE

• A's astonished reaction only makes sense after the confirming answer given in C, so C must precede A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Sajidah, who was then about seven, soon made friends with the new buffalo.

A. Such a friendship the little Sajidah had soon been able to make with the newcomer.

B. Of this attachment I shall soon give an example.

C. The large strong animal bends its head to the right, to the left, or downwards, just as the pressure of the child’s finger directs.

D. I purposely say “made friends,” for it was indeed touching to see how the buffalo was attached to the little boy who watched over and fed him.

S2: The buffalo turned willingly on reaching the end of the field, not losing an inch of ground when ploughing backwards the new furrow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, B, C, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Explaining the phrase ‘made friends,’ promising, then giving an example.

• D (the narrator's comment on the phrase ‘made friends’ used in S1) → B (‘this attachment’ refers to the bond just described in D) → C (the promised example from B — the buffalo's obedience) → A (a summarising remark on the example just given in C)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A promise to ‘give an example’ must be followed by that actual example.

 

NOTE

• C, the example, must directly follow B's promise, and A's summary comes only after the example.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Flaw Number Two is that deterrence is premised on fear.

A. On the contrary, it is the endless, tireless work of people who have the courage to openly denounce them.

B. It is not some inherent, mystical attribute of nuclear bombs that they automatically inspire thoughts of peace.

C. But fear is premised on knowledge.

D. On an understanding of the true extent and scale of the devastation that nuclear war will wreak.

S2: Deterrence will not and cannot work given the levels of ignorance and illiteracy that hang over our two countries like dense, impenetrable veils.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, D, B, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An argument that fear and peace depend on knowledge and active effort, not the weapons themselves.

• C (‘But’ immediately qualifies the claim about fear in S1) → D (explains what kind of ‘knowledge’ (from C) fear is based on) → B (denies that peace comes automatically, following the point in D) → A (‘On the contrary’ continues directly from B's denial, giving the true cause)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘On the contrary’ must follow the claim it is contradicting.

 

NOTE

• A's ‘on the contrary’ directly continues B's denial, so B must precede A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: As temperatures climbed, the trees proliferated and came into competition with each other.

A. Each banyan grew further, sometimes doubling back on itself for safety.

B. Under pressure, it evolved and adapted.

C. Always it grew higher and crept wider, protecting its parent stem as its rivals multiplied.

D. On this continent, the banyan gradually established ascendancy over other species.

S2: Their complexity became unrivalled, their immortality established.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, B, A, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The banyan's rise and adaptation amid plant competition.

• D (names the banyan as the specific example of the competition in S1) → B (‘it’ refers to the banyan just named in D) → A (continues describing how the banyan (B) adapted) → C (continues describing the banyan's growth pattern from A)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A pronoun like ‘it’ needs its noun named in the sentence immediately before.

 

NOTE

• B's ‘it’ refers to ‘the banyan’ named only in D, so D must precede B.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: In the village of Sittendorf in Germany there dwelt a poor but worthy man named Peter Klaus.

A. He could not have been persuaded for all the money in the world to spend his days in a shop tinkering at a trade.

B. He liked to be out of doors.

C. All the people for miles around knew Peter.

D. He was not fond of hard work.

S2: He liked to wander at his ease in the fields and woods, enjoying the sunlight and the flowers and the songs of the birds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, D, A, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Peter's reputation and character, especially his dislike of work and love of the outdoors.

• C (continues introducing Peter's reputation from S1) → D (‘He’ is Peter, continuing his character description from C) → A (elaborates on his dislike of hard work just stated in D) → B (contrasts with the dislike of shop-work in A, introducing what he did enjoy)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A general trait is usually followed by a specific illustration of it, then its contrasting preference.

 

NOTE

• A illustrates the dislike of hard work stated in D, and B's preference for outdoors leads into S2's continuation.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: My real life is the one nobody talks about anymore, except Father Paul LeBoeuf, another old buck.

A. But I can’t get him on a horse anymore.

B. His face is ruddy, and he jokes about being a whiskey priest, though he’s not.

C. He has a decade on me: he’s sixty-four, a big man, bald on top with grey at the sides.

D. He gets outdoors as much as he can, goes for a long walk every morning, and hunts and fishes with me.

S2: Ten years ago I could badger him into a trail ride; I had to give him a western saddle, and he’d hold the pommel and bounce through the woods with me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, B, D, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Describing Father LeBoeuf's appearance and habits, then a present limitation.

• C (describes Father LeBoeuf (‘He’), just named in S1) → B (continues physical and character description from C) → D (continues describing his (‘He’) active habits, from B) → A (‘But’ contrasts with the active outdoor habits just described in D)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘But’ introduces a limitation that must follow the habit it is limiting.

 

NOTE

• A's ‘can't get him on a horse anymore’ contrasts directly with the outdoor activity described in D, so D must precede A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: The word pronounced by the eccentric veteran seemed to have a magical effect on the rest of the company present.

A. Probably they had expected to profit by my intoxication.

B. When the old soldier returned and sat down again opposite me at the table, we had the room to ourselves.

C. Whatever their motive might be, at any rate they went away in a body.

D. With one accord they all rose to depart.

S2: I could see the croupier, in a sort of vestibule which opened out of it, eating his supper in solitude.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, A, C, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The company's sudden departure, its possible motive, and the aftermath.

• D (‘they’ (the company) react immediately to the word mentioned in S1) → A (the narrator's guess at their motive for departing, following D) → C (continues, regardless of the guessed motive in A) → B (describes the aftermath once the company had left, following C)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A guess at motive should follow the action it is trying to explain.

 

NOTE

• A's guess about their motive for leaving follows the departure described in D, so D must precede A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: For several weeks before Christmas, my father worked after supper in the cellar of our house.

A. My brother Laird and I sat on the top step and watched.

B. The naked, slippery bodies were collected in a sack and buried in the dump.

C. My father removed the pelt inside-out from the body of the fox.

D. The cellar was whitened and lit by a hundred-watt bulb over the worktable.

S2: One time the hired man, Henry Bailey, had taken a swipe at me with this sack, saying, “Christmas present!”
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, A, C, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The setting of the cellar work, the watching children, and the father's task.

• D (describes the cellar setting from S1) → A (the narrators' position, watching within the setting just described in D) → C (the specific action they watched, following the scene-setting in A) → B (the result of the pelt removal in C)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A description of the setting typically precedes who was watching and what was done.

 

NOTE

• C's specific action follows the scene set in D and the watchers introduced in A, and B follows directly from C.
